articles.title: This IPL Team Almost Had Hardik Pandya Before PBKS, But MI's Demands Stalled Deal: Report
articles.description: Hardik Pandya Trade: Hardik Pandya's move away from Mumbai Indians could have taken him to a different IPL franchise before Punjab Kings entered the picture. Rajasthan Royals reportedly came close to securing the all-rounder, but negotiations broke down after MI made a significant demand involving two key players. Hardik's future had become a major talking point after Mumbai wrapped up their IPL 2026 ninth on the table. According to Times of India, RR were seriously pursuing the India all-rounder and had emerged as frontrunners at one stage. Rajasthan Royals Made Strong Push For Hardik According to the TOI report, RR's ownership representatives and Director of Cricket Kumar Sangakkara travelled to Bengaluru to work towards completing the deal. The negotiations, however, reportedly hit a roadblock when Mumbai Indians outlined their conditions. MI are said to have wanted England fast bowler Jofra Archer and India opening batsman Yashasvi Jaiswal included in the proposed exchange, with them unwilling to send Hardik to Rajasthan without Archer being part of the package. RR did not agree to those terms, bringing the discussions to an end. Also Check || WATCH: Shoe Thrown At Krunal Pandya In Wankhede Stadium After SMAT Match Hardik Pandya's return to MI in 2024 as captain, replacing Rohit Sharma, had not delivered the expected results. The five-time champions missed out on the playoffs in two of the three seasons under his leadership. The eventual outcome was a trade to Punjab Kings in exchange for fast bowler Arshdeep Singh. Jofra Archer's Importance For RR Rajasthan Royals will head into the next auction with Rs 27.05 crore available, the fourth-lowest purse among the 10 teams, having retained big names like Jofra Archer and Yashasvi Jaiswal. Archer's retention is particularly notable given his previous association with both franchises. The England pacer began his IPL career with Rajasthan, had a brief stint at Mumbai Indians before returning to RR. Across the last two seasons, he has claimed 36 wickets in 28 matches for the Royals, being their top wicket-taker in 2025 and 2026.

articles.title: Former CSK Star And U19 World Cup Winner Retires At 32
articles.description: Baba Aparajith, a member of India's 2012 Under-19 World Cup-winning team, has brought his first-class cricket career to an end at the age of 32. The Tamil Nadu-born all-rounder announced his decision through an Instagram post, bringing the curtain down on a red-ball journey that spanned 102 matches and included more than 5,000 runs. However, this is not necessarily the end of his association with competitive cricket. Aparajith's retirement announcement specifically concerns first-class cricket, while reports indicate that he has registered for the IPL 2027 auction as he looks to explore opportunities in the T20 format. His final first-class appearance came on January 24, 2026, against Chandigarh while representing Kerala. He had moved to Kerala after spending most of his domestic career with Tamil Nadu. Baba Aparajith's Emotional Retirement Message Announcing the decision, Aparajith reflected on the teams he had represented and the people who had contributed to his career. "I played my last First Class game on 24th January 2026, and with that my First Class career has officially come to an end. Looking back, it has been an amazing journey filled with experiences, challenges, learnings, and friendships that I will cherish for a lifetime," he wrote. He also acknowledged the teams that gave him opportunities throughout his career, including Tamil Nadu, India Under-19, India A, Kerala, Chennai Super Kings and Rising Pune Supergiant. "It has been an absolute privilege to represent Tamil Nadu, India Under-19, India A, Kerala, Chennai Super Kings, Rising Pune Supergiant, TNPL franchises and my club teams, and to be part of the many teams and dressing rooms that have shaped my journey," Aparajith added. WATCH POST The 32-year-old also thanked the BCCI, the Tamil Nadu Cricket Association and the Kerala Cricket Association, along with his family, coaches, support staff and teammates. He made it clear that his connection with the sport would continue, expressing his desire to use the experience gained over the years to contribute to cricket in the future. From India's U19 World Cup Triumph To CSK's IPL Squad Aparajith was part of the Indian team that won the 2012 ICC Under-19 World Cup in Australia under Unmukt Chand's captaincy. His all-round performances played an important role in India's title-winning campaign. He finished the tournament with 171 runs and five wickets, emerging as one of the contributors to India's successful campaign. His performances in the knockout stages, particularly against New Zealand, helped bring him into the spotlight. His progress also earned him opportunities with IPL franchises. Chennai Super Kings signed him ahead of the 2013 season, and he was subsequently part of the Rising Pune Supergiant setup. However, he never made an appearance in an IPL match. Aparajith went on to build an extensive domestic career, representing Tamil Nadu and Kerala, while also turning out for India A. Across 102 first-class matches, he scored 5,199 runs, including 12 centuries and 27 half-centuries, and claimed 75 wickets. In List A cricket, he accumulated 4,278 runs and 83 wickets in 114 matches. His T20 record stands at 1,147 runs and 17 wickets from 63 appearances. Across the three formats, he finished with 10,624 runs and 175 wickets. While his first-class career has now reached its conclusion, the possibility of seeing Aparajith in the T20 circuit remains. His next chapter in cricket could yet take him back into the spotlight.
